subject: BlueHarbor: request for incident brief, IR plan, and SOC 2/SIG artifacts
messages:
From: Timothy Lee <security@blueharbor.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: aisha.patel@blueharbor.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: IRP & SIG/CAIQ artifacts + brief on recent auth anomaly

Hi Soojin,

We're running an internal due diligence after a short-lived auth anomaly we observed yesterday impacting a small subset of BlueHarbor sessions. Legal is looped for timeline sensitivity. To complete our security assessment and close the risk review we'd like the following from Redwood by EOD Friday (US pacific):

- A concise incident brief describing what you observed (timeline, affected surface)
- Redwood's Incident Response Plan (IRP) or an excerpt showing owner roles and escalation paths
- SIG/CAIQ or equivalent control artifacts for authentication and logging controls
- If available, a small redacted log sample showing the anomalous event (no PII)

We understand some items may be sensitive — a secure upload link is appreciated. If there's a SOC 2 report or attestation you can share under NDA, that would expedite legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Timothy Lee
Head of Security
BlueHarbor Capital

Attachments: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Lee <security@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: IRP & SIG/CAIQ artifacts + brief on recent auth anomaly

Timothy — thanks for the note and the clear list of asks. We're looking into the anomaly and can provide what you've requested. A few quick clarifications to make sure we deliver only what's needed:

- Redacted logs: we can provide sampled entries for the affected auth path (token exchange + IP/agent metadata only). Confirm that added redaction policy (no user identifiers) meets your needs.
- SIG/CAIQ: we maintain an internal mapping; we can export the controls for AuthN/AuthZ, Logging, and Incident Mgmt. Do you want the full SIG matrix or just the Auth/Logging slices?
- SOC 2: we can share our latest attestation PDF via a secure link; will require a short NDA if BlueHarbor needs the full report.

Plan and timelines from our side:
- Today: initial triage summary and scope (short brief)
- Tomorrow morning: redacted log sample + control excerpts (SIG slices)
- Friday: full IRP excerpt and SOC 2 attestation link (if NDA in place)

I'm looping Marissa (security ops) and Karthik (IR lead) to coordinate artifacts and to propose a 30-min sync tomorrow 9:30am PT if that works for BlueHarbor.

We will use the secure upload here: https://redwood-secure-upload.company/s/blueharbor-123 for any artifacts you prefer us to drop.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: none

Soojin — thank you. The redaction approach you propose is acceptable. For SIG/CAIQ, please prioritize the AuthN/AuthZ and Logging controls first; we may circle back for the full matrix.

Two items from legal:
1) If SOC 2 full report is being shared, Legal wants a stamping clause or an NDA before receiving. We'll send a standard mutual NDA if needed.
2) BlueHarbor is also evaluating SLA credits if the anomaly is determined to be a service reliability issue. Please include any relevant SLA metrics/uptime windows in the brief.

Also — if you can include a very short root cause hypothesis and immediate mitigations planned, that'll help our internal risk committee.

Thanks — can you confirm the 9:30am PT sync tomorrow? Aisha will join.

—Tim

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor incident brief, IR timeline excerpt and artifacts — upload link provided

Timothy / Aisha — following our triage and IR runbook steps, please find the initial artifact set and brief below. We've kept this high level; we'll share a fuller postmortem after our internal RCA completes next week.

Incident brief (summary):
- Detection: 2028-03-21 23:42:19 UTC — telemetry flagged a spike in failed token introspections for a small customer cohort (0.08% of auth requests)
- Impact: transient auth failures led to 14 affected sessions across two tenant IDs; no escalation to data exfiltration identified
- Cause (interim hypothesis): race condition in token cache invalidation during a background refresh rollout; reproduced in staging with increased load
- Mitigation applied: rollback of the background refresh change and a short hotfix to add stronger cache locking (deployed 2028-03-22 03:10:00 UTC)
- Current status: stabilized; monitoring continues with elevated thresholds and alerting for 72 hours

Artifacts uploaded to secure link (redwood-secure-upload):
- redacted_ir_timeline.pdf (summary timeline, owner list)
- blueharbor_s3_sample_logs.zip (redacted auth logs, sample entries)
- SOCT2_Attestation_2027.pdf (latest SOC 2 Type II attestation — redacted public version)

Key notes:
- We redacted user identifiers and payloads from the log samples per your request; logs retain timestamps, request metadata, and token exchange status codes.
- The IRP excerpt includes escalation owners, expected RTO windows for production auth, and our post-incident communication plan. If you need the full IRP (operational checklists), we can provide that under NDA.
- SLA metrics: our rolling 30-day auth endpoint availability was 99.995%; affected window lasted ~7 minutes. We included the relevant monitoring graphs in the redacted_ir_timeline.pdf.

Next steps:
- We propose a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow 9:30am PT to walk through the artifacts and answer questions. Please confirm.
- Formal postmortem with root-cause analysis and action plan to follow by 2028-03-29.

Thanks for the quick coordination — Marissa will host the sync and Karthik will present the root-cause write-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

- blueharbor_s3_sample_logs.zip
